as_told.title: Christopher Dunn's work on the pyramid's engineering anomalies

plain: This story is about the claim that the ancient Egyptians at Giza had better tools than history books say. Mario Woods, a former guard at a nuclear site who was a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, relays the work of an engineer named Christopher Dunn. Woods says the tools needed to carve and cut the granite there are not among the copper and wooden chisels archaeologists have found. Michels, the host, mentions Dunn more generally, as someone who has studied "engineering anomalies" in the Great Pyramid itself. If true, it would mean the builders had a lost technology.
